thread:
Ella M: Heads up — we need a concrete plan for distributing the ref-arch + Terraform modules to cloud partners. goal: make it frictionless for marketplace teams and SI partners to pick up samples and infra.
Dan P: +1. main things to nail: packaging format, versioning scheme, CI gating, and marketplace manifest generation.
Hao L: also provider compatibility matrix (aws provider versions, gcp beta api caveats, azurerm breaking changes). we should ship a small matrix with every release.
Sophie R: suggestion: publish modules to our public module registry + produce marketplace-ready bundles (zip + manifest) for each marketplace. registry for devs, bundles for partner marketplace ingestion.
Mike G: agree. propose pipeline: unit tests -> smoke deploy (tiny infra) -> module publish -> bundle build -> sign artifacts -> notify partners. estimates: 2x weekly runs for canary.
Ella M: can we add a quick checklist for partners so they know which bundle to pick (example stacks, terraform versions, required cloud services)?
Dan P: yes. checklist items: supported provider semver, example workspace, minimal IAM roles, estimated cost, known limits. also a "pitfalls" note for large seq_len models (cost spikes) — for SI docs.
Hao L: CI details: use GH actions matrix for providers. example step:
```
- name: run smoke deploy
  run: terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
```
use ephemeral creds via OIDC, then run acceptance tests.
Sophie R: marketplace-bot: please confirm manifest requirements for AWS Marketplace (AMIs vs containers), GCP Marketplace (cloudbuild yaml), Azure (ARM template + marketplace cpks).
marketplace-bot: AWS requires image/AMI or container + CloudFormation/CloudFormation schema for listing. GCP accepts a deployment manager or container image + marketplace listing metadata. Azure needs ARM or managed application package and publisher settings.
Mike G: we should keep two release channels: stable (tagged semver) and partner-beta (early bundles for SI). partner-beta bundles include experimental optimizations (quantized kernels, special routing) and a very clear "do not use in prod" note.
Ella M: naming convention idea: redwood-refarch/<cloud>/<version>/v{semver}-bundle.zip. manifest named metadata.json with keys: providers, tf_versions, example_stack, checksum, signed_by.
Dan P: signing: HSM/KMS sig or at least GPG for initial phase. partners prefer KMS-backed signatures though.
Hao L: add automated compatibility test matrix artifact: CSV with results for provider versions and hw variants (x86, arm64, a100, h100). publish alongside bundle.
Sophie R: deliverables for next week: 1) sample bundle prototype for AWS with metadata.json, 2) CI workflow that builds + smoke deploys, 3) partner checklist doc stub. owners: Dan (CI + publish), Hao (compat matrix), Ella (partner checklist + messaging).
Mike G: timeline ok. I'll coordinate with infra to reserve small test accounts for smoke runs.
Ella M: ok. one more: include an "upgrade path" note for partners — how to migrate from v1 -> v2 modules when breaking changes happen.
Dan P: noted. also track telemetry hooks (optional) so partners can opt into usage telemetry for optimizations.
Sophie R: thanks all — i'll set up a short demo for partners after we have the AWS prototype. target demo: 10 days.
Hao L: I'll add a small script to generate metadata.json from module outputs.
marketplace-bot: Reminder: attach required publisher agreements before submitting to marketplaces.
Ella M: great. meeting to sync on deliverables tomorrow 10am PT. :thumbsup:
